name: Australian Patience
description: Australian Patience is a strategic solitaire game that blends the layout of Klondike with the move-logic of Scorpion. It is characterized by having all tableau cards face-up from the start, requiring the player to build down in suit. Unlike Klondike, any cards sitting on top of a card being moved are carried along, making it a game of foresight and column management.

history.origins: Originating in Australia as a more skill-based alternative to Klondike. It gained international popularity in the digital era as part of high-difficulty solitaire collections.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Variations of open-layout solitaire emerge in the UK and Commonwealth.
1990s: Inclusion in early computer solitaire packages alongside Scorpion and Yukon.
Present: Recognized as one of the 'top-tier' strategic solitaires due to its low luck factor compared to Klondike.
history.cultural: Favored by competitive solitaire players who enjoy 'solvable' puzzles where defeat is usually the result of a misplay rather than a bad shuffle.
history.evolution: The game simplifies the 'hidden card' mechanic of Klondike by making everything visible, which shifts the challenge from discovery to optimization.

setup.players: One player for the standard solitaire game. The player shuffles and deals their own tableau; there is no dealer or opponent. Australian Patience can also be played competitively by two players (each with their own 52-card pack and tableau), but the primary form documented here is single-player.
setup.dealing: 7 columns of 4 cards are dealt face-up, slightly overlapped. This uses 28 cards. The remaining 24 cards form the draw pile (stock).

rules.objective: Move all 52 cards to the four foundation piles, organized by suit from Ace to King.
rules.gameplay: 1. Deal: 7 columns of 4 cards each, face-up (28 cards). Stock = 24 cards. 2. Play: Build tableau down in suit only. Move cards (and any cards on top) to other columns or to foundations. Flip stock one at a time to waste; top of waste is playable. 3. Foundations: Aces up in suit (A-2-3...K). 4. Win when all 52 cards are on foundations.
keyRules: Suit Building: You MUST follow suit in the tableau (unlike Klondike's alternating colors).
Visibility: All 28 starting cards are visible; use this to plan 3-4 moves ahead.
No Redeal: If the stock is empty and no moves remain, the game is lost.

strategy.basic: Prioritize exposing and moving Aces to the foundations immediately. Without your Aces, you cannot clear any cards.
strategy.intermediate: Column Management: Avoid creating empty columns unless you have a King ready to move into it. An empty column with no King is a wasted space that could have held card sequences.
strategy.advanced: Look-Ahead Analysis: Since all cards are face-up, identify 'Blocks'. For example, if the 5 of Hearts is trapped under the 7 of Hearts, you must find a way to move the 7 before you can ever play that 5.
tips: The 'No Redeal' rule makes every card in the waste pile precious. Don't flip a stock card if you have a viable move on the tableau.
Try to keep your tableau sequences 'pure' (uninterrupted suit order) to make them easier to move later.

variations.name: Competitive Australian
variations.description: Two players play with their own decks. The first to clear their foundations wins.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation describes the two-player competitive format; core engine remains shared with the solitaire version.

scoring.description: Standard solitaire scoring (points per card moved to foundation) or simple win/loss.
scoring.winCondition: Clearing the tableau and stock into the foundations.

synthesis.shortDescription: A sophisticated 52-card solitaire that challenges you to plan several moves ahead. With all tableau cards visible, the game is no longer about luck, but about precise suit-building and column strategy.
